# Independent audit: nonnegative marginal uniform domination

Audit of `candidate 5618a0288085d16a`.
Result: PASS, with no mathematical correction requested.

The hypotheses are a full-dimensional compact convex body in dimension
`d >= 1` and a nonconstant affine marginal `Y` with minimum zero. Its
law is nonatomic, its support is the whole interval `[0,b]`, and each
proper cut has mass strictly between zero and one.

Both cap-volume roots are concave on the actual support interval by
their respective Minkowski inclusions. At a proper cut `t`, writing
`alpha=F(t)` and `q=(1-alpha)^(1/d)`, the lower-root chord gives
`F(s) >= alpha (s/t)^d` for `0 <= s <= t`. The upper-root secant
inequality gives `1-F(s) <= [1-(1-q)s/t]^d` for `t <= s <= b`.
Applying that same secant inequality at `b` indeed gives
`b <= t/(1-q)`, so the affine bracket cannot become negative on the
support. Extending the resulting bound by its positive part is valid;
no concavity of a zero-extended root is asserted.

Integrating these two bounds yields exactly

    mu/t <= [d + q^d/(1-q)]/(d+1).

After multiplication by `alpha`, the numerator is

    d(1-q^d) + q^d (1+q+...+q^(d-1)) <= d.

This checks the coefficient, direction, and strictness for `d >= 2`
at proper cuts. The full-mass endpoint is handled independently:
the chord `F(s) >= (s/b)^d` gives `mu <= db/(d+1)`, which proves
the claim at `t=b` and for every `t>b`. The zero endpoint and the
uniform `d=1` case are also covered exactly.

An increasing cone has `F(s)=(s/b)^d` and
`mu=db/(d+1)`. It attains the coefficient at `t=b`; a longer
comparison uniform interval would retain a strictly positive upper
tail there while the original marginal has zero mass there. This
certifies sharpness of the universal interval length, not merely
sharpness of a sufficient intermediate estimate.

For a positive normalized simplex normal, the mean is
`r/(d+1)`, so the comparison interval is `[0,r/d]` with density
`d |T_d| r^(d-1)`. Its payment at the actual simplex centroid is
only `|T_d|r^d/(d+1)`. The note explicitly retains this loss and
does not infer the sharp mixed depth bound from the uniform comparison.

Validation: `python3 supporting computation verify_nonnegative_convex_marginal_cdf.py`
passes all 5268 exact checks. These arithmetic checks supplement the
all-body Brunn--Minkowski proof above.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
